chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from a man who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When the menstruating woman performs Tawaf, then she intends to bid farewell to the House, so let her stand at the nearest door from the doors of the Masjid, and let her bid farewell to the House.
ai.seo_question: Where should a menstruating woman stand to bid farewell to the Kaaba after completing Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* outlines the practical accommodation for a menstruating woman performing *Tawaf al-Adha* (Farewell Circumambation), permitting her to bid farewell to the Kaaba from the nearest door of the Masjid al-Haram rather than inside the sanctuary. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*rukhas*) in ritual purity, distinguishing between the validity of the act and the location of its completion. It reflects the broader jurisprudential principle that minor impurity (*hadath asghar*) does not invalidate the core ritual but may affect its optimal performance space.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Ali Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Hammad, from a man who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘When the menstruating woman performs Tawaaf, then she intends to bid farewell to the House (Kabah), so let her stand upon the nearest door from the doors of the Masjid, and let her bid farewell to the House (Kabah)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from a man who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘A woman experiencing Hayd (menses) who has performed Tawaf then wants to say farewell to the House, should stand near any of the doors of the Masjid and say farewell to the House.’”
